certificate.title: Trust this certificate
certificate.description:
For a certificate no public authority issued, like Home Assistant's self-signed one: its
SHA-256 fingerprint, or your certificate or CA certificate as PEM. Enter `none` to stop
trusting it.

commands.title: Let Irori control devices
commands.description:
On by default: Irori can switch, unlock, disarm and send commands through Home Assistant,
and Automations flows can do the same. Turn it off for a read-only try: Irori then only
reads Home Assistant and answers every command "read-only".

exclude_areas.title: Leave out these areas
exclude_areas.description: Never bring over entities in these areas (by name).

exclude_integrations.title: Leave out these integrations
exclude_integrations.description: Never bring over entities of these integrations.

include_areas.title: Also bring over these areas
include_areas.description: Also bring over every entity in these areas (by name), as for integrations above.

include_integrations.title: Also bring over these integrations
include_integrations.description:
Also bring over every entity of these integrations (`hue`, `zha`, `mqtt`…), even ones
Irori leaves out by default: those on no device, and hidden ones. Disabled entities never
come over.

resolves_locally.title: This name resolves locally
resolves_locally.description:
Turn on if this `https://` address is a public name that your network's DNS points at
Home Assistant's local address. Irori then connects only if it resolves to a local one.

token.title: Access token
token.description:
A long-lived access token of an administrator: in Home Assistant, your profile →
Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. An administrator's, because only
they can read Home Assistant's devices, areas and entities.

url.title: Home Assistant address
url.description:
Home Assistant's local address, as you open it in a browser on this network:
`https://homeassistant.local:8123`, or `http://` if it doesn't use a certificate.

x-irori-warn.text: Not encrypted: your Home Assistant administrator's access token travels unencrypted on your local network. Use https:// if your Home Assistant has a certificate.
